Part 2
📊 Standard Charts (1–10)
Core visualizations covering goals, assists, ratings, fitness, and discipline across players and teams.
Chart 01 · Horizontal Bar
Top 10 Goal Scorers
The top scorer leads by a significant margin. Top 3 scorers account for ~25% of their team's total goals, confirming that individual brilliance drives team success in the knockout stages.
Tableau: Player_Name → Rows | SUM(Goals) → Columns | Sort Desc | Top 10 Filter | Horizontal Bar
Chart 02 · Grouped Bar
Goals & Assists by Position
Forwards dominate goals while midfielders lead in assists — a clear tactical specialization. GKs and DEFs contribute minimally to direct goal actions, as expected.
Tableau: Position → Columns | AVG(Goals) + AVG(Assists) → Rows | Measure Names → Color | Side-by-Side Bar
Chart 03 · Histogram
Player Rating Distribution
Most players cluster between 4–7. Only ~8% achieve Elite status (≥8.5). The mean is skewed downward by reserve/bench players who see limited minutes.
Tableau: Player_Rating → Columns | COUNT(Player_ID) → Rows | Bar mark | Add Reference Lines at mean & 8.5
Chart 04 · Bar Chart
Pass Accuracy by Position
Midfielders average the highest pass accuracy (~88%), reflecting their build-up role. GKs average lowest (~72%) due to long distribution kicks under pressure.
Tableau: Position → Columns | AVG(Pass_Accuracy_Pct) → Rows | Fix axis 60–100 | Add Labels
Chart 05 · Scatter Plot
xG vs Actual Goals — Clinical Analysis
Points above the diagonal outperform their xG (clinical finishers). Points below are wasteful. This is the gold standard metric for striker evaluation in modern football analytics.
Tableau: xG → Columns | Goals → Rows | Position → Color | Add Reference Line (y=x) | Filter: FWD + MID
Chart 06 · Bar Chart
Distance Covered by Top 15 Teams
High-press teams cover significantly more ground — a quantitative marker of tactical intensity and physical conditioning. Teams that press hard tend to win more loose balls.
Tableau: National_Team → Columns | SUM(Distance_Covered_km) → Rows | Sort Desc | Top 15 Filter
Chart 07 · Bar Chart
Yellow Cards by Position
Defenders receive the most yellow cards — indicative of last-ditch challenges and tactical fouls. Midfielders follow, often used to break up dangerous counter-attacks.
Tableau: Position → Columns | SUM(Yellow_Cards) → Rows | Position → Color
Chart 08 · Line Chart
Goals by Tournament Round
Goals peak in the Group Stage (most matches). However, the per-match goal rate rises in later rounds as stakes increase. Semi-Finals and Finals produce the most dramatic scoring moments.
Tableau: Round_Reached → Columns (Custom Sort) | SUM(Goals) → Rows | Line Mark | Area fill
Chart 09 · Scatter Plot
Shots on Target vs Goals
Strong positive correlation between shots on target and goals. Players maintaining a conversion rate above 40% are elite clinical strikers — the rarest commodity in international football.
Tableau: Shots_on_Target → Columns | Goals → Rows | Position → Color | Filter: Shots > 2
Chart 10 · Horizontal Bar
Top 10 Goalkeepers by Saves
Elite GKs averaged 6+ saves per match — proving that world-class goalkeeping was equally decisive as clinical finishing. Defence wins tournaments just as much as attack.
Tableau: Player_Name → Rows | SUM(Saves) → Columns | Filter: Position = GK | Top 10 | Horizontal Bar
Part 3
🧮 7 Calculated Fields
Each calculated field includes the Tableau formula, step-by-step setup, inference (what the chart shows), and interpretation (what it means strategically).
1
Performance Tier Classification
IF THEN ELSE — Conditional Calculated Field
Formula
IF [Player_Rating] >= 8.5 THEN "Elite"
ELSEIF [Player_Rating] >= 7.0 THEN "Standard"
ELSEIF [Player_Rating] >= 5.5 THEN "Below Average"
ELSE "Poor"
END
Tableau Setup
Analysis → Create Calculated Field → Paste formula → Name: Performance Tier → Drag to Columns | COUNT(Player_ID) → Rows | Performance Tier → Color
Inference
Only ~8% of all players achieve Elite status (Rating ≥ 8.5). The Standard tier (7.0–8.5) forms ~35% of players. The Poor category (~30%) represents benched/reserve players with minimal minutes.
Interpretation
IF-THEN tiering is critical for squad analysis. Teams with 3+ Elite-rated players in their starting XI consistently outperform teams with 0–1 Elite players. This field becomes a primary KPI filter on the Executive Dashboard.
2
Continental Group
GROUP BY — Manual Group / Set
Setup Steps
Right-click [Continent] → Create Group
Name: "Continental Group"

Groups:
  Europe       → France, Germany, Spain...
  South America → Brazil, Argentina...
  Africa        → Morocco, Nigeria...
  Asia          → Japan, South Korea...
  CONCACAF      → USA, Mexico, Canada...
Drag Continental Group to Columns | AVG(Player_Rating) → Rows (Bar) | SUM(Goals) → dual axis (Line)
Inference
Europe has the highest average player rating but South America scores more total goals per team. Africa and Asia show the lowest ratings and goal totals, reflecting the global talent gap.
Interpretation
Continental grouping reveals philosophical differences in football culture. European football prioritises technical precision (high pass accuracy, team structure). South American football produces more clinical goal-scorers. Critical insight for scouting and tactical preparation before international fixtures.
3
Top 5 Teams by Goals
FILTERS — Top N Filter
Setup Steps
Drag [National_Team] → Rows
Right-click [National_Team] → Filter
→ Top tab
→ By Field: Top 5
→ Field: SUM(Goals)
→ Click OK
Apply Top N filter → Bar chart | SUM(Goals) → Rows | National_Team → Color
Inference
The top 5 goal-scoring teams are separated from the rest by a significant margin. All 5 teams reached at least the Quarter-Finals — confirming goal-scoring as the #1 predictor of tournament advancement.
Interpretation
Top N filters in Tableau are essential for executive dashboards where stakeholders need quick insights without information overload. This pattern should be applied across KPI tiles and leaderboards in all 3 dashboards to guide resource allocation decisions.
4
Age Group Bins
TABLEAU BINS — Continuous Measure Binning
Setup Steps
Right-click [Age] → Create Bins
Bin Size: 5
Name: "Age (bin)"

Resulting bins:
  17–20  |  21–25  |  26–30
  31–35  |  36+

Drag [Age(bin)] → Columns
AVG(Goals) → Rows | COUNT → dual axis
Inference
17–20: Avg 0.48 goals — raw talent, limited experience
21–25: Avg 0.78 goals — rising stars, high energy
26–30: Avg 1.12 goals — PEAK PERFORMANCE AGE ⭐
31–35: Avg 0.65 goals — physical decline, tactical wisdom
36+: Avg 0.20 goals — veteran role players
Interpretation
Age bins definitively identify 26–30 as the Golden Age for World Cup performance. Federations should plan player development cycles around this peak window. Teams with high concentrations of 26–30 year old forwards have statistically better goal-scoring outcomes.
5
Team Rating Excluding Goalkeeper
EXCLUDE LOD — Level of Detail Expression
Formula
{ EXCLUDE [Position] : AVG([Player_Rating]) }

Apply with filter: Position != "GK"

Result: Team-wide rating ignoring
positional context (outfield players only)
Create field → Drag to Rows | National_Team → Columns | Compare with All-inclusive average on dual axis
Inference
EXCLUDE LOD removes the position dimension from the level of detail. When GK is filtered, outfield averages for attacking nations (Brazil, Argentina, France) show a measurable uplift of 0.2–0.5 rating points vs all-inclusive averages.
Interpretation
EXCLUDE is the correct metric for comparing attacking squad quality across teams. By excluding GK position context, we isolate outfield player quality — the component that directly drives goals and match outcomes. Used in scouting reports to rank teams by outfield depth.
6
Player-Level Goals Within Position
INCLUDE LOD — Level of Detail Expression
Formula
{ INCLUDE [Player_Name] : AVG([Goals]) }

Adds player-name granularity to a
positional aggregation — exposes the
distribution WITHIN each position
Create field → Box Plot or Distribution Chart | Position → Columns | LOD field → Rows | Show distribution
Inference
Box plot reveals that even within Forwards, the top 10% score 5–7× the median Forward. Without INCLUDE, the Forward average (2.4 goals) completely masks this extreme skew. 50% of all Forwards score 0–1 goals.
Interpretation
INCLUDE LOD reveals that goal-scoring is heavily concentrated in a small elite cohort. This changes squad strategy: 1–2 elite Forwards are far more valuable than 5 average ones. Management should invest in acquiring one world-class striker rather than spreading budget across multiple average options.
7
Fixed Team Baseline Goals
FIXED LOD — Level of Detail Expression
Formula
{ FIXED [National_Team] : SUM([Goals]) }

Creates an UNCHANGING baseline for
each team — constant regardless of
what other filters are applied to the view
Create field → Bar chart | National_Team → Columns | FIXED LOD → Rows | Add Reference Line at global average
Inference
The FIXED value for each team remains constant even when position/age/round filters change the view. Teams shown in blue (above dashed orange line) are the tournament's dominant scoring teams. Baseline enables ratio calculations (e.g., % of goals from Forwards).
Interpretation
FIXED LOD is Tableau's most powerful aggregation tool. It creates an unchanging benchmark that persists through all dashboard interactions. When a user filters by "Forwards only," the FIXED team baseline still shows total team goals — enabling calculation of "% goals from Forwards" as a real-time ratio across all filter states.
Part 4
📈 5 Advanced Charts
Pareto, Waterfall, Donut, Dual-Axis Combo, and Trend Line Scatter — the most impactful chart types for executive storytelling.
Advanced 1 · Pareto Chart
80/20 Rule — Teams Driving Tournament Goals
Just 8 out of 46 teams account for 80% of all tournament goals — a textbook Pareto distribution. This confirms that elite teams define the tournament's attacking narrative and media coverage.
Tableau: National_Team → Columns (Sort Desc) | SUM(Goals) → Rows (Bar) | Duplicate → Dual Axis → Running Total → % of Total (Line) | Reference Line at 80%
Advanced 2 · Waterfall Chart
Cumulative Rating Build by Position
Each position adds cumulatively to the team's overall rating profile. Forwards contribute the highest incremental value, but the foundation built by GK and DEF is what enables overall team stability in knockout rounds.
Tableau: Position → Columns | Running SUM(AVG Rating) Calc → Rows | Mark type: Gantt Bar | Size by delta | Green (positive) / Red (negative)
Advanced 3 · Donut Chart
Player Distribution by Position
Midfielders form the largest positional group, reflecting modern football's tactical emphasis on midfield control (4-3-3, 4-2-3-1 formations). The 10% GK allocation is consistent — 2 GKs per squad minimum.
Tableau: Pie Chart → Position → Color | COUNT → Angle | Duplicate → Dual Axis → reduce inner size → donut hole | Center text annotation
Advanced 4 · Dual-Axis Combo
Total Goals (Bar) + Avg Rating (Line) by Team
High ratings don't always translate to high goals. Some top-rated teams play pragmatic defensive football. The dual-axis makes this disconnect immediately visible to non-technical stakeholders and coaching staff.
Tableau: National_Team → Columns | SUM(Goals) → Rows (Bar) | AVG(Player_Rating) → Rows → right-click Dual Axis → Line | Synchronize Axes | Format colours
Advanced 5 · Scatter Plot with Trend Lines
Minutes Played vs Player Rating — by Position
Strong positive correlation — players who play more minutes consistently earn higher ratings. The trend line confirms this is statistically significant (R > 0.6 across all positions). Top performers earn their playing time; playing time validates their performance.
Tableau: Minutes_Played → Columns | Player_Rating → Rows | Position → Color | Analytics pane → Trend Line → Linear → Per Color | Show R² and P-value
Part 5
🔮 Forecasting Chart
Exponential Smoothing applied to average player ratings across tournament stages, with 95% confidence interval projection.
Forecast · Line Chart with Exponential Smoothing
Average Player Rating by Tournament Stage — With 2-Stage Forecast
Average player ratings steadily increase as the tournament advances — players perform better under higher stakes. The forecast model (Exponential Smoothing, α=0.4, 95% CI shown in orange band) predicts peak ratings in the Final and Championship stages.

This validates the "big stage performance" theory — players who compete regularly in high-pressure environments systematically outperform their regular-season baseline ratings.
Tableau Steps: Round_Reached → Columns | AVG(Player_Rating) → Rows | Line Chart → Analytics pane → drag Forecast → Right-click → Forecast Options: 2 periods ahead, Exponential Smoothing, Show 95% Confidence Interval
